references.note: Approved disc, lighting and camera; do not copy its creature.
Native shape (64x64): a pale grey-white four-legged drake with long spread wings and an open mouth.
Shipped Rantha the Worm (pale silver-blue winged dragon coiled round): the ice element and every cold drake must not read as this pale coiled winged dragon.

prompt_fields.subject: A storm drake seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle: a lean slender mature drake stretched along a DIAGONAL from lower-left to upper-right, head thrown back and up with the jaws open and a forked yellow lightning bolt between the teeth, TWO LONG NARROW POINTED SWALLOW-TAIL WINGS swept back along the body like a jet, a long thin tail, deep royal-violet and indigo scales with a paler lavender belly, bright yellow lightning veins running across the wings and down the flanks, yellow eyes, slim clawed legs tucked in. Streamlined, electric and complete.
prompt_fields.contrast: Storm family: the ADULT storm drake is a LEAN DIAGONAL STREAK with two long narrow swept wings and a head thrown back, royal violet with yellow lightning veins (silhouette: diagonal narrow dart; hue: violet-indigo with yellow; value: mid-dark with bright yellow). The storm hatchling is a small reared T-shape; the fire drake is a wide delta with flame; the cold drake is a heavy round teal boulder; the venom drake is a broad green hunched body.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Disc plate discipline: measured results show generations of this style reference tend to render the disc DARKER than the reference, never lighter. So do not darken the disc at all: render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band and the area under the creature -- at the style reference's own brightness, if anything a hair lighter, and never darker. No warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette anywhere on the disc. Do not darken the creature to compensate either. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures. The ENTIRE creature, every limb, tail, wing, drip, staff and effect included, fits inside a circle of about three quarters of the disc radius around the disc centre, leaving a wide bare charcoal ring of base plate on every side, yet the creature is large and bold inside that circle. This is a dragon on a small tabletop disc, drawn COMPACT and chunky: wings, tail, neck and head are pulled in so the whole silhouette forms one rounded mass inside the inner three quarters of the disc; no wing tip, tail tip, claw, horn, drip or flame reaches the outer sixth ring band or crosses the disc rim. Do not spread the wings wider than about two thirds of the disc diameter. Calibration from the previous generation of this exact token: it passed the gate but at 48px the slim muted-violet body was thin and low-contrast against the charcoal disc. This time keep the same diagonal lower-left to upper-right pose, the head thrown back with a lightning fork in the jaws and the two long narrow swept wings, but make the drake noticeably BOLDER: a thicker chest and body and thicker wings, a clearly LIGHTER and more saturated periwinkle-violet hide (mid-light value, lit from the upper left), broad pale lavender wing membranes, and thicker bright yellow lightning veins and a bright yellow-white chest stripe, so the silhouette and the yellow accents stay readable at 48px. Still no larger than about three quarters of the disc radius.
prompt_fields.palette: Royal violet and indigo scales with lighter lavender highlight planes and belly, bright yellow lightning veins and eyes; nothing darker than dark indigo except the mouth; keep the body mid-value, not near-black; the lightning must not glow onto or tint the disc. Dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel, kept a visibly lighter value than the creature's darkest parts so the two never merge.
